editorial:
Imagine waking up every day knowing that your husband's job is one of the deadliest in the world. You are dropped right into the lives of women in Guatemala City who have lost their partners to street violence. These women weren't just wives; they were the backbone of their families while their husbands drove public transport vans and taxis. The vibe is heavy and honest, focusing on the raw pain and the strength these women find to keep going. It feels less like a polished movie and more like a real conversation with people who have survived the unthinkable.

What really hits home is how the director lets the women speak for themselves without adding too much fluff. The pacing is slow and steady, which helps you feel the weight of their grief. One downside is that it can be very sad to watch, so be prepared for an emotional ride. If you like true stories that show the side of the world we rarely see, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing that these women are still fighting for justice and support. There is no magic happy ending because the violence in Guatemala City continues, but you see the widows forming a community to help one another. The final scenes emphasize that while their husbands are gone, their struggle to survive and provide for their children is a daily battle that never truly ends. It leaves you thinking about the cost of a commute.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful true stories and social documentaries.
